segments.text:
`=== bwx12 read ===` is the header that build12.sh writes before the text of each kernel [Ref1]. `read` is the name of the kernel in the option `--seq` of bwx12. It is the new read kernel.
- The whole-chip test times this function in part C only [Ref9].
- Part A times the new read kernel in another binary, bw_new [Ref16].
segments.heading: Kernel `read`: the new read kernel, function `k_read`

segments.text:
Start address `49a0` (hexadecimal) and name of the function. **The loop is lines 4 to 14.**
- Address range: `49a4` to `49cc`. That is 11 instructions, 44 bytes of code. Loop start modulo 64: 36.
- Bytes read per loop pass: 256 B.
- Load instructions per loop pass: 8 (`ldp`, 32 B each).
- Other instructions per loop pass: 3 (`add`, `cmp`, `b.hi`).
- The loaded values are not used.
- Source: the `do ... while` loop of the C function `k_read` in bwx12.c [Ref2].

This instruction runs once per call, before the loop.
- On entry `x0` holds `a`, the address of the first byte to read. `x1` holds `n`, the number of 8-byte words to read.
- The instruction computes the end address `x1 = x0 + 8 * n` (`lsl #3` multiplies by 8). Source: `end = a + n`.

The loop starts at line 4. Each `ldp` (load pair) reads 32 B from memory into two vector registers of 16 B. The 8 instructions read the 256 B that start at `x0` (offsets 0 to 224 B). No instruction uses the loaded values.
- Source: 16 calls of `vld1q_u64` (the C function that loads one vector of 16 B). The compiler joined the 16 loads in pairs: each `ldp` does two of them.
- An empty `asm` statement in the source takes the 16 loaded values as inputs. The comment in bandwidth.c says that this keeps gcc from deleting the loads, and that it adds no instruction [Ref3].
`add x0, x0, #0x100` moves the pointer forward by 256 B (`0x100` = 256). Source: `p += 32` (32 words of 8 B). So one pass of this loop is one pass of the `do ... while` loop of the source.

`cmp x1, x0` compares the end address with the pointer. `b.hi 49a4` jumps back to line 4 while the end address is higher (unsigned compare). Source: `while (p < end)`. objdump adds the words after `//`: another name of the same branch condition.
`ret` returns to the caller. The function returns no value. Line 16 is the empty line that ends the block.
